metadata.summary: England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.

England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand. Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21. Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup. The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti. metadata.summary: Harry Cobden made his first ride on Jonbon in public a successful one as the odds-on favourite landed a third Shloer Chase in gritty fashion at Cheltenham.

Never out of the first two in 29 races, Nicky Henderson's charge is approaching veteran status at the age of 10 and was winning for the 21st time in his stellar career. His task was made easier with the late withdrawal of Gidleigh Park, but Mighty Bandit kept him honest after the last, with the 1-2 favourite pulling away again towards to line to win by two and a quarter lengths. Cobden said: "I'm so fortunate to be in this position riding all of these great horses and there's so many in the camp to look forward to, you do have to pinch yourself a little bit. "I was really looking forward to it and pressure is just something you put on yourself isn't it. There was no point having a sleepless night over a Shloer Chase though as what would I be like in March!" He went on: "I really enjoyed that. metadata.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between ‌six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and ‌dislocated thumb.
metadata.content: NFL: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson to miss up to 10 weeks with broken and dislocated thumb | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update NFL: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson to miss up to 10 weeks with broken and dislocated thumb Lamar Jackson will miss between ‌six and 10 weeks with a broken and ‌dislocated thumb; Jackson suffered the injury on his first play from scrimmage in Baltimore's 36-10 loss to Buffalo Bills; quarterback could still return this season should Baltimore make playoffs Friday 13 November 2026 16:20, UK Image: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between ‌six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and ‌dislocated thumb. Jackson suffered the injury on his first play from scrimmage in Baltimore's 36-10 loss to Buffalo Bills when his throwing hand was hit by pass rusher Greg Rousseau, but could still return this season if the struggling Ravens can get back into the postseason picture. "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal," said Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter. messages.text: England in losing habit after 'failing to adapt' in Perth drubbing

metadata.summary: England "weren't quick enough to adapt to the conditions" as they slumped to a seven-wicket loss to Australia in the first ODI of their three-match series in Perth, according to head coach Brendon McCullum.
metadata.content: Australia vs England: Brendon McCullum blames side's 'failure to adapt' in heavy first ODI defeat in Perth | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Australia vs England: Brendon McCullum blames side's 'failure to adapt' in heavy first ODI defeat in Perth England bowled out for 131 in 33.4 overs as part of seven-wicket drubbing by Australia in first ODI of three-match series at Optus Stadium; second match takes place in Adelaide on Sunday before concluding in Hobart, Wednesday - start times 3.30am, UK time Friday 13 November 2026 13:06, UK Image: Tom Banton trudges off after being dismissed by Xavier Bartlett as England were bowled out for 131 in Perth England "weren't quick enough to adapt to the conditions" as they slumped to a seven-wicket loss to Australia in the first ODI of their three-match series in Perth, according to head coach Brendon McCullum. Unlike their inadequate preparations for the Ashes Test tour last winter - which also started with a heavy defeat at the Optus Stadium - the tourists this time played a proper warm-up game at the comparably bouncey WACA in Perth, but despite the time spent acclimatising, they were bundled out for a mere 131 in 33.4 overs in the series opener. "It all happened pretty quick!" McCullum told TNT Sports after his side's heavy defeat, Australia knocking off the runs in 23.3 overs. "We weren't quick enough to adapt to the conditions.
